T: A2 [ T ] to no longer have something because you do not know where it is
A2 [ T ] to have something or someone taken away from you
B2 [ T ] to stop feeling something
B1 [ T ] to have less of something than you had before
B2 [ T ] If you lose time, you waste it.
› [ T ] If a clock loses time, it goes more slowly than it should.
› [ T ] informal to get rid of something

NONE: C1 A business that is losing money is spending more money than it is receiving.
虧損

I or T: B1 [ I or T ] to fail to succeed in a game, competition, etc.

example: I've lost my ticket.
我丟了票。
He's always losing his car keys.
他總是丟汽車鎖匙。
At least 600 staff will lose their jobs if the factory closes.
如果公司關閉，至少將有600名員工失去工作。
He lost his leg in a car accident.
他在一場車禍中失去了一條腿。
She lost her mother (= her mother died) last year.
去年她母親去世了。
to lose confidence/faith
喪失信心／信念
I lost interest halfway through the book.
這本書我剛讀了一半就沒了興趣。
He kept on crying and I lost my patience.
他哭個沒完，讓我失去了耐心。
I'm trying to lose weight.
我正在努力減肥。
He's losing his hair.
他在掉頭髮。
She lost a lot of blood in the accident.
她在事故中流了很多血。
to lose your memory/sight
失憶／失明
Four million hours were lost last year through stress-related illnesses.
去年與工作壓力相關的疾病導致了400萬小時工作時間的損失。
We lost valuable time stuck in traffic.
塞車浪費了我們寶貴的時間。
My watch loses ten minutes every day.
我的手錶每天慢十分鐘。
Lose the belt and let's see how the dress looks.
把帶子解下來，再看看裙子怎麼樣。
Banks will lose millions of pounds because of new legislation.
銀行將因新法規的實施而虧損數百萬英鎊。
If we lose this game, we're out of the championship.
我們如果輸掉這場比賽就會在錦標賽中出局。
They lost to Cincinnati.
他們輸給了辛辛那提隊。
Everyone hates losing an argument.
誰都不願意在辯論中輸掉。
They hadn't lost an election in 15 years.
在15年當中他們從未在選舉中失利。

NONE: C1 to become less popular or to be given less support
失寵；失去支援

example: Do you agree that left-wing politics are losing ground among the working classes?
你是否同意左翼政治觀點正在失去工人階級的支援？

NONE: C2 to stop believing that you can succeed
灰心，失去信心

example: Don't lose heart, there'll be plenty more chances for promotion.
別灰心，還會有很多晉升的機會。

NONE: › to stop being able to control your emotions and suddenly start to shout, cry, or laugh
失去理智；突然大叫（或哭、笑）

example: I'd been trying so hard to stay calm but in the end I just lost it.
我拼命想保持冷靜，但最終還是沒有控制住自己。

NONE: › to not have an advantage that other people have
處於劣勢；吃虧

example: The new tax means that the vast majority of working people will lose out.
徵收新稅意味著大多數正在工作的人將會受損失。

NONE: C2 to forget about an important idea or fact because you are thinking too much about other things
忘記，忽略
C2 to forget about an important idea or fact because you are thinking too much about other things
忽略；忘記

example: I'm worried that we're losing sight of our original objectives.
我擔心我們會淡忘我們的初衷。
Some members of the peace-keeping force seem to have lost sight of the fact that they are there to help people.
維和部隊的有些人員似乎忘記了他們到那裡是爲了幫助人們。

NONE: C2 to worry about something
擔心，憂慮

example: I wouldn't lose any sleep over what happened.
事已至此，我才不擔心呢。

NONE: › UK If a football manager loses the dressing room, the players no longer respect him or follow his instructions.
（足球隊總教練）失去權威

example: If the owner believes he has lost the dressing room, it could spell the end for the manager.
如果球隊老闆認為總教練失去了權威，這就意味著他要丟工作了。

NONE: › to no longer be able to act normally or understand what is happening
行爲怪異；舉止愚蠢

example: I can't believe Stuart did that - he must be losing the plot.
我無法相信這是斯圖爾特做的——他肯定是傻了。

NONE: lose track
B2 to no longer know what is happening, or not to remember something
忘記；跟不上最新的情況

example: What he was saying was so complicated that I lost track after the first couple of sentences.
他說的話內容太複雜了，我聽了開頭的幾個句子以後就跟不上了。
I've lost track of the number of times he's asked me to lend him money.
我記不起他有多少次問我借錢了。

NONE: C1 to lose control and not act in a calm way
失去理智；情緒失控

example: He usually stays quite calm in meetings but this time he just lost his head.
開會時他通常都很冷靜，但這次他卻很衝動。

NONE: › to fall in love with someone
愛上（某人）
B2 to die suddenly because of an accident or violent event
喪生，丟掉性命

example: Many people lost their lives in the floods.
許多人在洪水中喪生。

NONE: › to become mentally ill, or to start behaving in a silly or strange way
精神失常；失去理智

example: You just spent all that money on a pair of shoes? Have you completely lost your mind?
你把錢都花在這雙鞋子上了？你一點理智都沒有了嗎？

NONE: › to suddenly become very angry
發火，發怒

example: He said one too many stupid things and I just lost my rag.
他的蠢話說得也太離譜了，我終於忍不住發了火。

NONE: › to lose a lot of money, especially as a result of a bet (= money risked when you guess the result of something)
（尤指因賭博而）輸得精光
› If you lose your touch, you can no longer do something as well as you could before.
技藝大不如前，做某事的能力下降

example: It's good to see their goalkeeper's not losing his touch.
好在他們的守門員仍然保持了以往的水準。

NONE: › to become lost
迷路，走失
› A lose-lose situation or result is one that is bad for everyone who is involved.
對各方都不好的

example: He said that going ahead with the strike would be a lose-lose situation for all concerned.
他說如果罷工舉行的話，對各方來說都無益處。
Compare
win-win

C: › a person or team that does not win a game or competition
› informal a person who is always unsuccessful at everything they do
› someone or something that is in a worse position or has less value at the end of a process

example: The losers of both games will play each other for third place.
兩場比賽的負者將爭奪第三名。
He's a good/bad loser (= he behaves well/badly when he is defeated).
他是個輸得起／輸不起的人。
He's a born loser.
他天生就是個倒楣蛋。
The latest price increases mean that the real loser, as usual, is the consumer.
與以往一樣，最近這次漲價的真正受害者還是消費者。

C or U: B2 [ C or U ] the fact that you no longer have something or have less of something
B2 [ C or U ] the death of a person
S: C2 [ S ] a disadvantage caused by someone leaving or by something being taken away
C: C1 [ C ] a situation in which a business spends more money than it earns

NONE: › an occasion when a number of people die
喪生，死亡

example: Many parents feel a sense of loss when their children leave home.
孩子們離家後許多父母都會有失落感。
He suffered a gradual loss of memory.
他的記憶力越來越差了。
There will be substantial job losses if the factory closes down.
如果工廠關閉，大批工人將會失業。
blood/hair/weight loss
失血／脫髮／體重減輕
It would be a great loss to the department if you left.
你如果離開將是該部門的巨大損失。
They never got over the loss of their son.
他們一直沒有走出失去兒子的陰影。
The company announced a pre-tax loss of three million dollars.
公司宣佈稅前虧損300萬美元。
The plane crashed with serious loss of life.
飛機失事導致很多人遇難。

NONE: › a person who works for an insurance company and decides how much money should be paid out in each case of something having been damaged or lost
（保險公司的）損失評估師，損失估價員
› an article that is sold cheaply in order to attract the public and make them buy other, more expensive, things
（用來招攬顧客的）低價商品
› not making a profit
虧損的，不盈利的
› not involving the loss of data or electrical energy
沒有丟失資料的，沒有損耗電子能量的

example: Lossless compression algorithms reduce file size with no loss in image quality.
無失真壓縮演算法可以減少文檔大小卻不影響圖像品質。
Compare
lossy

NONE: › involving the loss of data or of electrical energy
丟失資料的；損耗電子能量的

example: Lossy file compression results in lost data and quality from the original version.
有損檔案壓縮會丟失原始文檔和數據的品質。
Compare
lossless

NONE: A2 not knowing where you are and how to get to a place
迷路的，走失的
B1 If something is lost, no one knows where it is.
丟失的，失蹤的
C1 not confident and not knowing what to do in a particular situation
不知所措的，迷惘的
› giving so much attention to what you are doing that you are not conscious of anything else that is happening around you
投入的，沈迷的

example: I got lost in the New York subway system.
我在紐約地鐵裡迷路了。
You look lost - can I help you?
你好像迷路了——我能幫你嗎？
Things tend to get lost when you move.
搬家時東西常常會不知去向。
Lost: black cat with white paws.
尋貓啓事：黑貓，白爪。
Mikey turned up with the lost book.
米基帶著丟失的那本書來了。
It was his first day in the office and he seemed a little lost.
他那天是第一次來辦公室上班，看上去有點不知所措。
Ann was completely lost in her book.
安完全沈浸在她的書裡了。

NONE: › someone or something that has no chance of succeeding
沒有希望的人（或事）

example: I used to try to get him to do some exercise but then decided he was a lost cause.
我曾試圖讓他運動運動，但後來覺得他真是無可救藥。

NONE: › If something or someone gets lost in the shuffle, that thing or person does not get the attention they deserve.
未得到應有的重視；被忽視

example: Refugee children in the big camps just get lost in the shuffle and are sometimes left without food.
難民營裡的兒童沒有得到應有的重視，有時甚至連吃的都沒有。

NONE: › personal objects that have been left by accident in public places
遺失物品
› a place in a public building where things that people have lost are stored
失物招領處
› a place in a public building where things that people have lost are stored
失物招領處
